title: Opportunistic prefetch + lazy decode scheduler sketch
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight engineering sketch proposing an opportunistic prefetch + lazy decode flow that aims to improve tail latency and GPU utilization for mixed workloads. It explores a hybrid scheduling approach that overlaps token prefill work with selective early decode execution, backed by KV cache residency heuristics and microbatching knobs.

Context and motivation:
- We have two dominant phases: prefill (encode/prefix processing + KV cache population) and decode (autoregressive token emission). Current strict separation wastes device time when pipelines are imbalanced: short decodes wait on long prefill slots and vice versa.
- Microbatching increases throughput but can inflate latency for high-priority interactive streams.
- KV cache residency and freshness are key: moving KV data between memory tiers is expensive; we should avoid needless evictions.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile end-to-end latency for interactive streams by 15–30% on mixed workloads.
- Keep GPU occupancy within 60–95% depending on SLO targets (configurable).
- Avoid >3% regression in mean token cost compared to baseline batching strategy.
- Prevent KV thrashing: reduce cross-epoch eviction rate by 25%.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Models have long context (8k+ tokens) and KV working sets can be large — residency decisions matter.
- We operate on shared GPU pools with multiplexing across customer tiers.
- The serving runtime supports fine-grained kernel selection per op and can preempt or reorder per-slot work at microbatch boundaries.

High-level design idea:
1) Opportunistic prefetch: prefetch embeddings/KV data for upcoming queries earlier than strict prefill boundary when slot idle budget exists. Prefetch is best-effort and can be low-priority.
2) Lazy decode: start partial decode kernels (short-window beam/next-token passes or logits-only kernels) for streams once a minimal KV prefix is available, but stop before final token emission until higher-priority checks pass. This allows decoder kernels to overlap with remaining prefill I/O or heavier attention recomputation.
3) Hybrid priority lanes: maintain 3 lanes — realtime (interactive), throughput (batchy), background (prefetch/caching). Scheduler promotes/demotes slots across lanes based on observed latencies, remaining token budget, and customer SLA.
4) KV residency scorer: each slot has a KV-residency score computed from recency, expected future reuse (modelled from prompt/metadata), and memory cost. Use this to bias prefetching and to avoid evicting high-score entries.
5) Microbatch elasticity: dynamically tune microbatch size per lane. Realtime lane uses smaller microbatches with aggressive preemption; throughput lane uses larger microbatches for kernel efficiency.

Scheduler sketch (textual algorithm):
- Input: ready_slots queue with slot metadata (priority, remaining_prefill_tokens, estimated_decode_tokens, kv_score, SLO_deadline).
- At each scheduling tick:
  1. Compute idle_budget for each GPU (time quantum not committed).
  2. For high priority realtime slots with minimal prefill left (<K tokens), allow lazy-decode start: allocate decoder kernel where kv_score >= threshold or prefetch can complete within latency window.
  3. If idle_budget > low_watermark, pull one background prefetch job (opportunistic) and mark its IO as low-priority (cancellable).
  4. For throughput slots, accumulate until microbatch_target reached or deadline approaching; dispatch fused kernels.
  5. Enforce KV-residency guardrail: if eviction risk for high-score KV entries > limit, throttle background prefetch and promote corresponding slots to higher priority to keep KV hot.

Notes on lazy decode mechanics:
- Lazy decode must be deterministic and reversible: any decoder work performed speculatively must be idempotent or checkpointed so we can reuse partial compute once full KV is present.
- Practically, we run a logits-only pass (lightweight matmul-only kernels) that computes next-token logits for a window; full attention recompute is deferred and overlapped with remaining prefill IO.
- If subsequent prefill changes KV (e.g., additional context tokens), we recompute only affected layers/shards; this is why kernel-level dependency tracking is necessary.

KV cache management ideas:
- Sharded residency map: keep hotness counters per KV shard, decayed over time. Use a small hardware-friendly LRU approximation rather than full LRU.
- Reserve a fraction of GPU memory (configurable) for high-score KV entries (pin list). Eviction-only from pin list requires explicit promotion/demotion and operator approval.
- Opportunistic prefetch writes go to a staging area; actual KV residency commit happens only when downstream decode starts or the slot is promoted. This reduces thrash.

Microbatching policy examples:
- Realtime lane: max_microbatch = 4 tokens per kernel, preemption_latency_target = 10ms, batching window = 2ms.
- Throughput lane: max_microbatch = 64 tokens per kernel, no preemption, batching window = 15ms.
- Background lane: batch size tuned to fill idle cycles, aggressive cancellation allowed.

Operational safety and rollback plan:
- Start as opt-in runtime mode behind a feature flag (opportunistic_lazy_decode=true).
- Canary on Dedicated pools with non-critical customers for 1 week. Metrics to monitor: per-slot tail latency, kernel compute overlap fraction, KV eviction rate, GPU utilization, error/recompute rate due to speculative results.
- Fallback behavior: if any metric regresses > threshold (configurable), auto-disable speculations and drain existing background prefetches.

Experiment plan (short-term):
- E1: Microbench on single-GPU rig with synthetic workload mix (70% throughput, 30% interactive). Measure latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, prefetch cancellation rate.
- E2: Real-customer traffic A/B on dedicated pool (10% traffic). Collect KV eviction traces and compute cost delta.
- E3: Kernel-level profiling to verify speculative logits pass is <20% cost of full decode pass.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity: increased scheduler complexity may introduce bugs and makes reasoning about worst-case latency harder.
- Determinism: speculative decoder results must not diverge between runs; need to handle RNG/seeding carefully for sampling decodes.
- Memory fragmentation: staging + pin lists may increase fragmentation; need compaction strategies.
- Model differences: some architectures may not support cheap logits-only passes — need per-model capability flags.

Implementation milestones (rough):
- M0 (2w): telemetry and simulation harness to estimate benefits on historical traces.
- M1 (4w): lightweight KV-residency scorer + background prefetch task and cancellable IO primitives.
- M2 (6w): lazy logits-only kernel path + dependency tracking for partial decode reuse.
- M3 (4w): priority lanes in scheduler + microbatch elasticity controls.
- M4 (2w): canary rollout + dashboards and automated rollback triggers.

TODOs (who/when):
- Priya: build simulation harness with past 30 days traces (due 2025-02-28).
- Julian: prototype cancellable prefetch IO and staging commit (due 2025-03-07).
- Maya: design logits-only kernel integration and layer checkpointing API (due 2025-03-14).
- Avery: implement scheduler primitives and a simple policy config (due 2025-03-10).

References and related work:
- Internal: RUNTIME-512 (batching heuristics), RUNTIME-678 (kv eviction telemetry).
- External: literature on speculative execution in CPU schedulers and async prefetch in DBs for inspiration.

Appendix: quick failure scenarios & mitigations:
- Scenario: speculated decode diverges because prefill later changes prompt tokenization. Mitigation: detect tokenization changes early and abort speculative path; fall back to standard prefill->decode pipeline.
- Scenario: background prefetch overwhelms PCIe and increases p95. Mitigation: implement adaptive backoff tied to observed PCIe utilization.

Summary:
This sketch trades modest implementation complexity for potential improvements in tail latency and utilization via overlapping prefill and decode with careful KV residency management. Next step is to validate with simulation on representative traces; if results are promising, iterate with a focused engineering spike to get cancellable IO and a minimal logits-only decode path into the runtime.

-- end --
